newsitem.title: UK: Sterling debt and futures closing report.
newsitem.headline: Sterling debt and futures closing report.

text.p: Gilts ended slightly in the red on Wednesday, giving up early gains as Bunds and T-bonds backtracked.
Dealers said all eyes are now on retail price data for March, due at 0830 GMT on Thursday. The June gilt future settled 2/32 lower at 109-22 with barely 50,000 contracts changing hands.

"If T-bonds had broken 107-00 seriously, gilts would have gone much lower," a LIFFE floor broker said. "As it is, gilts are still quite a good sell at the moment. We could see 108s by the end of the week."
The June T-bond future dropped as low as 106-29 after a strong set of U.S. industrial production and capacity utilisation figures, but later clawed back up to 107-05.

Headline retail prices are forecast to jump 0.4 percent in March, leaving the year-on-year inflation rate unchanged at 2.7 percent. Underlying inflation, excluding home loan payments, is forecast to edge down to 2.8 percent year-on-year, from 2.9 in February.
"We think hopes of a further fall in inflation could be frustrated this month," said Jonathan Loynes, UK economist at HSBC Markets.
"A number of the erratic components that helped the fall in February (particularly seasonal food prices) could work in the opposite direction," he said.

Tuesday's welter of data showed a 41,100 fall in unemployment, annualised average earnings growth of 5.0 percent and a 1996/97 public sector borrowing requirement of 22.8 billion stg, well below the government's 26.4 billion forecast.
Andrew Snowball, Cooperative Bank economist, said the numbers were broadly positive with the PSBR actually undercutting market forecasts.
The June gilt reached a high of 109-30 shortly after the data but did not hold those giddy heights for long with Bunds, and later T-bonds, heading south.
The gilt/Bund spread held stock still at 184 basis points as the UK market continues to find outperformance hard to come by.

The June short sterling future, which settled unchanged at 93.43 on Wednesday, has gained about 20 basis points over the last week, as the market has started to scale back its expectations for rate rises.
At 93.43, the market is not even pricing a half-point rise in base rates by the end of June.
